newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks close lower despite strong Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks close lower despite strong Dow.

text.p: Leading European stock markets closed lower on Friday despite a storming performance on Wall Street, undermined by tax worries in London and profit taking on continental bourses.

On the foreign exchanges, the dollar was robust due to data showing strong U.S. first quarter economic growth and continuing worries about the single European currency, but economists doubted it could climb much further.

Wall Street's surge pulled European markets off their day's lows. But investors showed little of the enthusiasm which pushed the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 70.79 points or 0.92 percent to 7,725.04 by the European close.

Among the continental markets, Germany and France closed modestly lower as they consolidated after record closes on Thursday, while London was down almost 0.4 percent as dealers fretted about a government budget next Wednesday.

In London, the FTSE-100 index halved its earlier losses but still closed down 17.6 points at 4,640.3, albeit 45 points up on the week. "We are not so much running up to the budget but stumbling," one trader said.

Investors were worried about how finance minister Gordon Brown would try to control surging consumer spending to avoid domestic interest rate rises, and whether his tax plans would be biased towards the corporate sector.

"If it's a tough budget which comes down hard on the consumer sector with a net fiscal tightening to the tune of about three to five billion sterling it will be taken well by the market," said Jeremy Batstone, head of research at NatWest Stockbrokers.
"If it's a mild budget then we will worry about base rates having to go up," he added.

Brown will also unveil the size and scope of a windfall tax on privatised utilities which the Financial Times suggested would amount to a hefty five billion pounds ($8 billion). British Telecom, which is seen paying out up to one billion pounds, closed down seven pence at 448.5.

In Paris shares regained most of their earlier losses as the market consolidated after hitting successive highs which took the CAC Index to 2,900. The blue-chip index closed just below the key level, down 2.60 points at 2,891.04.
Rhone-Poulenc fell 4.44 percent to 241.3 francs on profit taking after rising almost 20 percent on Thursday due to the possibility it would buy out its U.S. unit Rorer.
In Germany an end-of-month, pre-weekend lethargy set in and the DAX index closed down 9.88 points at 3,795.41.

Traders still forecast the recent rally could resume and the DAX index could hit new record highs in the coming weeks. But some said the DAX would probably take a breather before U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers meet on Tuesday and Wednesday next week to discuss interest rates.
"People are playing the market cautiously because of the Fed meeting and also because it's hard to predict these days what Wall Street is going to do," said one Frankfurt trader.
"The losses look like a small bout of profit-taking," said another trader. "The institutional buyers will be back next week."

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was firm with the strong U.S. gross domestic product data and the Wall Street surge helping it to 1.7372 marks, its highest level since June 17. It was at 1.7265 late on Thursday.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported that GDP had risen a revised 5.9 percent in the first quarter, the economy's most robust performance in nearly nine years.
The resulting optimism also pushed the dollar to a European high of 114.61 yen, against 113.22 on Thursday, but economists doubted the dollar would keep climbing.

"The Japanese authorities would like to see dollar/yen stable and the U.S. authorities won't want the dollar to get too high," said Adrian Schmidt at Chase Investment Bank. "At levels above 115.00 it will start to look difficult."
The dollar was also helped against the mark due to continuing worries about the single European currency.

Dealers are awaiting the meeting of the Federal Open Markets Committee on July 1 and 2 but higher U.S. rates are not expected. "It would be a huge shock if the FOMC meeting led to anything," said Robert Hayward at Bank of America.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 114.61 yen and 1.7372 marks compared with 113.22 yen and 1.7265 marks in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 17.6 points at 4,640.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 2.60 points at 2,891.04.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 9.88 points at 3,795.41.
PRECIOUS METALS AT CLOSE
Gold was at $336.35 after an afternoon fix at $336.55 an ounce, the lowest since April 1, 1993, and compared with $338.15 at Thursday's close. Silver was at $4.73.
